incident_type: Compromised Root Infrastructure / Fraudulent Wildcard Issuance
description: Intrusion into DigiNotar CA systems resulted in rogue wildcard certificates for google.com and other domains, leading to full root distrust across all major browser vendors.
advisory: Distrusted Certificate Authority. Root anchor revoked across all modern operating systems.

incident_type: Backdated SHA-1 Certificates and Unauthorized Domain Issuance
description: Failure to enforce baseline validation requirements and intentional backdating of certificates to bypass SHA-1 deprecation led to distrust by Mozilla, Google, and Apple.
advisory: Distrusted Certificate Authority. Certificates must not be trusted for public web traffic.

ca_name: Free Automated DV CA (Phishing Abuse Context)
incident_type: Automated Domain Validation Exploited by Threat Actors
description: Free DV certificates are automated and domain-validated only; over 80% of active phishing portals employ free DV certificates to display HTTPS padlocks.
references: https://www.apwg.org/trendsreports/ - APWG Phishing Activity Trends Report
advisory: A valid TLS certificate from an automated DV provider confirms encrypted transport, but provides zero validation of site legitimacy or identity.
